tasks.short: Monitor office machines and make necessary adjustments

steps.what: Watch actual machine operation, inspect output and read the machine's displayed status or fault indicators
inputs: actual running office machine and its output
machine's own status indicators
outputs: operator's actual operating observations and displayed status

steps.what: Diagnose the observed operating problem and choose the exact safe adjustment or decide to stop for service
inputs: operator's actual operating observations and displayed status
machine operating instructions and permitted operator adjustments

steps.what: Apply the selected machine adjustment and check the resulting output, or stop the machine as selected
inputs: operator-selected adjustment or stop decision
actual office machine
outputs: actual adjusted or stopped machine and checked output

tasks.design: Configure the existing status display in {OTHER}, the office machine control panel, to keep available fault and consumable information visible. The operator still observes the real output, chooses the adjustment and applies it; no remote machine control or new sensing is assumed.
tasks.previous_blocker: Available status information may require repeated panel navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native control-panel views can expose existing status directly.
tasks.still_hard: Paper movement, output quality and safe physical adjustments need local observation.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when a displayed status does not explain the actual fault.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: office machine control panels can display native status while physical output monitoring and adjustments remain operator work.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human effort, not machine runtime or measured baselines.
OTHER means the existing office machine control panel. The machine itself produces the status indicators; no missing telemetry or new structured capture is assumed.
Only repeated navigation within s1 changes. Physical inspection, diagnosis and adjustment remain fully retained.
Gross provisional saving 3.25 minus 1 hour of checking display configurations gives 2.25 net; existing equivalent views give zero additional saving.
Each adjustment is selected by the operator before execution; a different setting requires a new decision.
unknowns: Available panel settings and actual navigation effort
research_questions: Can native status configuration remove repeated panel navigation without reducing output checks?

already_counted.description: Observe output/status, diagnose faults and apply selected adjustments

incremental.description: Check native display settings after machine or firmware changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 2.25%; all physical monitoring remains and native views may already be configured.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Clean and repair office machines and report major faults

steps.what: Inspect and clean the actual machine and perform only permitted minor repairs
inputs: actual machine condition
machine cleaning and operator-repair instructions
outputs: cleaned machine, actual repair results and unresolved major fault observations

steps.what: Write and check the major-repair report with actual machine identity, symptoms, displayed fault and minor work already attempted
inputs: cleaned machine, actual repair results and unresolved major fault observations
existing machine asset record
outputs: complete checked major-repair request and internal recipient

steps.what: Submit the completed major-repair request to the internal service desk
inputs: complete checked major-repair request and internal recipient

tasks.design: Configure the existing machine asset lookup and fault-report form in {HELPDESK} so the operator can reuse actual asset identity while describing observed symptoms. Cleaning and minor repairs remain physical work, and the completed report is checked before the separate internal submit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repair reports may require re-entering known asset details.
tasks.enabler_now: Native asset-linked service forms can reuse those details.
tasks.still_hard: Cleaning, repair competence and safe escalation require direct inspection.
tasks.human_edge: Distinguish a permitted minor repair from a fault that needs a technician.

ambition.what: No expansion of repair authority assumed.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: asset-linked service forms can reuse machine identity while operators supply actual fault observations.

assumptions: Shares describe an unmeasured maintenance episode requiring the report explicitly named in the task; routine cleaning without a major fault has no report saving.
Existing asset records are maintained by the asset owner. The operator supplies symptoms, fault indication and attempted repair during s2; these are not inferred from a maintenance plan.
No extra report approval step is introduced: s2 includes ordinary final checking. Internal submission remains fully retained.
Gross provisional saving 1.9 minus 0.5 hour of form/asset-link upkeep gives 1.4 net; existing prefill yields zero additional saving.
unknowns: Current fault-report channel and asset links
research_questions: Do actual repair reports re-enter asset information that native forms can reuse?

already_counted.description: Describe actual symptoms and check the completed repair report

incremental.description: Check asset lookups and fault-report form fields

approvals.approved_version: complete checked major-repair request and internal recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 1.4%; applies only to real reports with repeated asset entry.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain office-machine supplies and requisition needed stock

steps.what: Physically inspect and count actual supplies and determine what stock is needed for the machines' work
inputs: actual supply stock and machine requirements
known upcoming machine work
outputs: operator's actual supply counts and needed items

steps.what: Find the compatible approved supply items and current pack sizes and terms in the procurement catalogue
inputs: operator's actual supply counts and needed items
existing approved procurement item records

steps.what: Complete and check the requisition for the quantities actually needed
inputs: operator's actual supply counts and needed items
checked compatible supply item records

steps.what: Submit the completed checked requisition through the existing internal procurement route
inputs: complete checked supply requisition

steps.what: Move available supplies to the machines and replenish their supply compartments
inputs: operator's actual supply counts and needed items
actual available supply stock

tasks.design: Configure machine-compatible catalogue favourites and item-field prefill in {PROCUREMENT}. The operator still checks physical stock, enters actual needed quantities and checks the final requisition before submitting it internally; physical replenishment is a separate unchanged step.
tasks.previous_blocker: Finding compatible items and re-entering catalogue fields can accompany physical supply work.
tasks.enabler_now: Native procurement favourites and item prefill can reuse existing catalogue records.
tasks.still_hard: Physical counts and actual work needs cannot be inferred from a reorder threshold alone.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise substitutions, unusual demand and supplies that will not work in a particular machine.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: procurement favourites and item prefill can shorten catalogue navigation and entry without replacing physical stock checks.

assumptions: Shares are provisional and unmeasured, not a claim of current administrative effort.

Procurement staff already maintain item identity, compatibility, pack size and terms. The operator produces actual counts and required quantities; no new stock ledger or inferred consumption is assumed.
Only catalogue navigation and fixed item-field entry change; all physical replenishment remains. No automatic supplier order is proposed.
Gross provisional saving 3.2 minus 1 hour of favourites/compatibility upkeep gives 2.2 net. Existing equivalent favourites/prefill remove the gain.
The final submit is negligible and fully retained; procurement approval follows the completed requisition.
unknowns: Current procurement configuration and compatible-item coverage
research_questions: Which actual supply requisitions still require repeated catalogue search or item entry?

already_counted.description: Check catalogue options and complete/check the requisition

incremental.description: Maintain machine-compatible favourites and item mappings

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 2.2%; physical stock work is unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and process papers for scanning or microfilming

steps.what: Inspect and organise the actual papers, remove fasteners and prepare fragile or irregular pages for the chosen capture process
inputs: actual paper documents and capture instructions
outputs: physically prepared paper batch with preserved page order

steps.what: Set the appropriate capture settings, load and operate the scanner or microfilm equipment
inputs: physically prepared paper batch with preserved page order
actual capture instructions and equipment
outputs: actual captured image or film batch

steps.what: Check captured pages for order, completeness and legibility and correct or recapture failures
inputs: actual captured image or film batch
physically prepared paper batch with preserved page order

steps.what: Save or release the completed checked capture batch to the existing document destination
inputs: complete checked capture batch

tasks.design: Configure the native batch thumbnail and page-order view in {OTHER}, the document-capture application, for scanned-image work. Physical preparation and capture stay unchanged, and the operator checks completeness and legibility before releasing the exact checked batch to {DOCS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Opening captured pages individually can slow completeness and order checks.
tasks.enabler_now: Native thumbnail views can show existing captured pages together.
tasks.still_hard: Fragile paper handling, missing pages and unreadable originals require physical attention.
tasks.human_edge: Know when an image looks plausible but has lost meaningful content or order.

build_days.consent_and_access: 0-2 for capture settings and document permissions

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: document-capture applications can display native batch thumbnails to support page checking without replacing physical paper preparation.

assumptions: Shares are provisional human work, not scanner runtime. OTHER means scanner or microfilm capture controls/application.
The operator creates the actual batch in s2; no unexplained structured page manifest or automatic content classification is assumed.
The view only affects digital-image navigation within s3; microfilm-only equipment without an equivalent view has zero saving.
Gross provisional saving 1.9 minus 0.5 hour of view-setting upkeep gives 1.4 net. Existing batch views remove the gain.
Every page still needs the required quality check; same-system save/release remains fully retained.
unknowns: Digital versus film workload and current batch views
research_questions: Does a native thumbnail view remove repeated page opening while preserving the required quality checks?

already_counted.description: Inspect capture quality and correct or recapture failures

incremental.description: Check batch-view settings after capture-profile changes

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Below provisional net 1.4%; film-only work or existing thumbnails give no change.
